agent_response.summary: Candidate 1 is ready for evaluation, but it is not the combination I was assigned. I could not read the source of Astra revision 7d1ccc5: my file tools are confined to this worktree, there is no shell, and .git points outside it. I did not author a combination I couldn't verify. Instead I submit a separate hypothesis of my own, based only on 7d1ccc5's recorded phases (forward compile 7.6→3.3 s, gradient compile 2.0→4.1 s, same execute times). That pattern looks like residual work moved from the forward vjp into the backward pass. The change is a new flag, ASSEMBLY_REMAT=True, in differometor/simulate.py, which wraps the per-row assembly lax.map body in jax.checkpoint(prevent_cse=False). build.py is unchanged from aa2b1ab. Setting the flag to False restores aa2b1ab behaviour.
agent_response.hypothesis: Target phase: forward compile, 7.62 s in full job 35abe628 (aa2b1ab), 35% of the first run. Mechanism: the forward stage compiles jit(vjp(simulate)). In the 101-row "assemble" lax.map, the residuals of every grouped component function are emitted as stacked per-row scan outputs. Rematerializing the loop body makes the forward scan save only its inputs; the reverse scan recomputes the assembly per row. Prediction: forward compile and lower go down, gradient compile and lower go up, and gradient execute rises by an unknown recompute cost. The net total is unknown; 7d1ccc5's phase pattern is an analogy, not evidence for this code. Numerics: forward outputs should stay bitwise identical, because the primal ops are the same and the solves are untouched. The gradient should stay near 4.5e-13. Any forward difference or a strict gradient failure (index 161) rejects the candidate.
agent_response.notes: Notes are in experiments/notes/claude-guided-v2.md. The owned combination (aa2b1ab + 7d1ccc5) is BLOCKED because 7d1ccc5's source cannot be read with the sandboxed tools. To unblock it, the coordinator needs to deliver the exact 7d1ccc5 diff and its parents into this worktree, for example under experiments/context/. Candidate 1 is my own remat hypothesis, not a code transfer. Scientific parent: aa2b1ab only; 7d1ccc5 is cited as phase-pattern motivation only. Source delta: simulate.py only (ASSEMBLY_REMAT flag plus a checkpoint wrap of block_assemble). Fallback: ASSEMBLY_REMAT=False. Please run a full evaluation and include the strict comparison; any improvement would need matched confirmation against aa2b1ab.
